About the neighborhood — and why Strivers’ Row is special:

Strivers’ Row (officially the St. Nicholas Historic District) is a landmarked block of late 19th-century rowhouses protected by the New York City Landmarks Preservation Commission and listed on the National Register of Historic Places. The brownstones here have been owned by the same families for generations — this is not a transient block. It’s a genuine community with deep roots and real neighbors who look out for each other. West Harlem has transformed significantly and continues to thrive, but Strivers’ Row in particular has always been a safe, quiet, residential enclave — tree-lined, grounded, and proud.
